Subject: Secure-site deployment discovery — recap & technical asks

Hi Elena + team,

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of the items we covered and the technical questions we need to close to size an on-prem / VPC-hosted, air-gapped deployment for MedHCP. I captured pain, goals, and constraints below.

What you told us (pain / goals):
- Patient data residency: all PHI must remain within MedHCP-controlled network and storage.
- Compliance drivers: internal audit plus state-level health data rules require full audit logs and 7 years retention.
- Offline / air-gapped compatibility: preferred for high-risk clusters; at minimum, outbound-only NAT enforced via proxy.
- Low latency for clinician workflows (<= 120ms token latency target for core prompts).

Key constraints we noted:
- No inbound public IPs allowed to the inference servers.
- Egress must go through corporate proxy; TLS termination on your side.
- KMS requirement: customer-managed keys (HSM) or AWS CloudHSM equivalence.
- Strict IP allowlist for any callback / webhook endpoints.

Open technical questions / asks (please confirm):
1) Can we run within your VPC with only outbound connectivity (NAT + proxy) and no inbound ports?
2) Will MedHCP provide an internal package mirror (or allow our offline packages via approved media) for initial deployment?
3) Do you have a preferred HSM vendor (YubiHSM, AWS CloudHSM, Thales) and an operations contact for key rotation policy?
4) Which SIEM do you ingest audit logs into? What format / retention settings are required beyond 7 years?

Next steps and owners:
- Vivek: draft a minimal architecture options doc for (a) fully air-gapped install, (b) VPC outbound-only install — target by Mon 05 Oct.
- Jordan: circulate a Mutual Action Plan (attached) and proposed SOW template; follow up on procurement timeline.
- Elena / IT: confirm answers to the 4 technical questions above and share any networking diagrams.

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_MedHCP_v1.xlsx (MPA), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, networking-diagram-medhcp.png

Thanks — looking forward to the answers so we can size the Dedicated/on-prem pricing and schedule a proof-of-concept.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive

From: Dr. Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medhcp.com>

Cc: MedHCP IT <it-ops@medhcp.com>, procurement@medhcp.com
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Secure-site deployment discovery — recap & technical asks

Jordan — thanks for the clear write-up. Short answers inline below:  

1) Yes, outbound-only via NAT + proxy is our preferred topology. No inbound traffic to compute nodes.
2) We do not host a general package mirror. We can accept vendor-delivered media (signed tarballs) after SCA. Prefer an initial deliverable via our secure file transfer (SFTP-to-airgap) process.
3) We use AWS CloudHSM today; rotation policy is quarterly. Operations owner: Miguel Torres (miguel.torres@medhcp.com).
4) SIEM: Splunk Enterprise; retention: raw logs 7 years, indexed alerts 3 years. We will need the audit events in JSON/NDJSON with timestamped token/meta fields.

We'll review the MPA and loop in procurement for timeline (likely 8–10 weeks procurement + 4 weeks staging).

Elena Ruiz, MD
Chief Medical Information Officer
MedHCP

Subject: Re: Secure-site deployment discovery — technical notes

Thanks — quick technical clarifications from our infra side:  

- Outbound-only topology is supported. For model updates we propose a signed artifact workflow: Redwood prepares container images & model bundles, signs them, and MedHCP pulls via SFTP or approved USB after verification. We can provide an automation script to validate signatures and verify hashes.
- KMS/HSM: we can integrate with AWS CloudHSM or accept external HSM-backed keys via PKCS#11. We will need an OIDC client for the control-plane auth; that can be scoped to internal network only.
- Audit logs: Redwood will emit NDJSON with structured fields: timestamp, model_id, request_id, user_id (hashed), token_count, latency_ms, error_code. We can also push to an on-prem Splunk HTTP Event Collector behind your allowlist.

Action items I will own:
- Draft signed-artifact delivery flow + verification checklist (target Mon 05 Oct).
- Produce minimal Egress/IP list for allowlisting (includes our update broker and telemetry endpoints) — note: these endpoints can be static FQDNs or fixed IPs via peering.

Vivek
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
